title: test design flaky tests coverage limits and maintainability
concepts: Test quality depends on whether the suite distinguishes correct behavior from plausible defects, not on the number of test files or the percentage of lines executed.

A test pyramid is a planning heuristic: fast isolated tests are numerous, broader integration tests are fewer, and end-to-end tests focus on critical user journeys. A rigid ratio is not a substitute for architecture and risk analysis.

A flaky test passes and fails without a relevant code change. Retries can expose flakiness but do not fix its cause; diagnose shared state, timing, concurrency, external dependencies, data collisions, and environment assumptions.

Line and branch coverage show which code ran, not whether assertions checked meaningful outcomes. Mutation testing introduces realistic code changes and checks whether tests detect them; surviving mutants guide investigation, not automatic test additions.

Property-based testing generates many inputs against a general invariant and shrinks failures to a smaller counterexample. It complements hand-picked examples, especially for boundary-heavy algorithms and parsers.

Snapshots are useful when the serialized output itself is the contract and reviewers can understand changes. Large opaque snapshots often hide meaningful regressions and should be replaced with focused assertions.

Maintainable suites use clear test names, deliberate data, isolated setup, meaningful assertions, and stable abstractions. Tests should be refactored with production code while preserving the intended behavioral contract.

items: Microsoft.Testing.Platform code coverage uses Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage; VSTest and MTP have distinct configuration and command-line surfaces, so examples must match the selected runner.
MSTest 4.4 reports retry attempts and identifies flaky/retried tests in run summaries; use retries as diagnosis evidence, not as a substitute for fixing nondeterminism.
Current Stryker.NET requires the .NET 10 runtime or newer to run; the tested application may target an earlier framework. Set up the tool runtime separately from the application target.

accuracyFacts: Code coverage measures executed code such as lines, branches, or methods; it does not establish that assertions detect incorrect behavior.

Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage with Microsoft.Testing.Platform excludes the test assembly by default. VSTest and Microsoft.Testing.Platform have different coverage setup and command-line surfaces.
A fixed coverage output path can overwrite per-module reports in a flat results layout. Preserve distinct reports before merging; a later merge cannot recover files already overwritten.

Stryker.NET's mutation score denominator includes killed, timed-out, survived, and no-coverage mutants; mutants that error are excluded from the score. A survivor is a prompt to investigate whether behavior is asserted or the mutant is equivalent/unreachable, not an automatic instruction to add a test.

Equivalent mutants produce no observable behavior change for the relevant program context and cannot be reliably identified automatically in every case; investigate survivors rather than assuming they expose a missing assertion.

FsCheck properties use generators and shrinkers; the failing input is reduced while it continues to falsify the property. Default test counts/configuration can be changed, and failures can report a seed for replay.
A custom FsCheck shrinker may re-run a property multiple times. Properties over mutable generated state must rebuild/reset that state so shrinking does not observe prior mutations.

MSTest TestContext.CancellationToken is available starting with MSTest 3.11 and is signaled on timeout or test-run abort. Cooperative cancellation requires test code to observe/pass the token; otherwise timed-out work may continue.
MSTest 4.4 and Microsoft.Testing.Platform report retry attempts and identify retried/flaky tests in the run summary; process-level retries and method-level retries can multiply executions.
Retries, quarantine, and numeric quality gates can improve diagnostics or manage risk temporarily, but they do not repair nondeterministic tests or prove behavior by themselves.
Test pyramids and test trophies are planning metaphors, not universally correct test-count ratios. Select layers based on behavior, failure risk, fidelity, diagnostic value, and maintenance cost.

“Microsoft Code Coverage” is a tooling family: VSTest uses its built-in Code Coverage data collector, while MTP uses the separate Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage package and MTP command options. The instruction must match the selected runner.
